claims.text: In Edo State, once a tenant applies to the Rent Tribunal, any quit notice served afterwards has no effect under section 16.

post.headline: A dispute at the tribunal pauses your quit notice
lines: In Edo State, once a tenant applies to the Rent Tribunal,
any quit notice served afterwards has no effect under section 16.
A landlord cannot use a retaliatory notice to force you out while the tribunal is hearing your case.
Know your rights before an agent uses threats to push you out.
post.cta: Which state are you renting in? Tell us below, and follow for the next rule.

threads.text: In Edo State, filing a matter before the Rent Tribunal stops any retaliatory quit notice under section 16. The landlord cannot issue a notice while the tribunal decides. Has your landlord ever threatened you with eviction after a simple complaint?
threads.evening: In Edo State, retaliatory quit notices have no legal weight once the dispute is before the tribunal.

why: Sunday engagement question using the CLAIM hook on Edo's strong s.16 anti-retaliation protection, obeying the 5-word question and follow orders.
